title: Ceallach is born in the high valleys
summary: A son is born to Gille-Brìde's brother of Somhairle's line in the high valleys and is called Ceallach; he is slower to walk and to run than the children before him, the first sign, told back afterward, that the years were coming down faster in him than in his father.

title: A woman of Clann na Ceiste speaks over the child
summary: An old woman of Clann na Ceiste, come down from the slab to see the new child, tells Gille-Brìde that a boy born short-lived among the long-lived will learn early what his own kin have never needed to learn until late: how much of a life can be made to matter in however much of it is given.

title: Fearghal Donn dies at Dùn dhearg
summary: Fearghal Donn, who had held Dùn dhearg since before Niall Òg was sent to him and sent back with nothing, dies an old man in his own bed at the fort; the households east of the vein bury him as they buried Ailis, without word sent to the hill and none expected back.

title: Artair takes up the holding of Dùn dhearg
summary: Artair, Fearghal Donn's son, takes up the holding of Dùn dhearg with no more ceremony than his father had used, and says at the burying itself that he will hold what his father held and ask nothing further of the hill until the day it asks something of him.

title: Gille-Brìde's father dies in his three hundred and eighth year
summary: Gille-Brìde's father dies at Samhain in his three hundred and eighth year, fewer years than his own father had, dying as most of that line has learned to die: without illness or wound, simply slower each year until one morning he does not rise from his own hearthstone.

title: Word runs that the kin will gather below Dùn ìseal
summary: At the burying, word runs among the fires that the king's kin mean at last to come down out of their scattered holdings and gather in the valley below Dùn ìseal, each line with its own tents and its own fire, to wait together upon the shares left uncounted since Catrìona Mhòr's death.

title: The kin come down household by household
summary: Through the summer the king's kin come down into the valley below Dùn ìseal household by household and line by line, no single word sent to call any of them, until the valley holds more tents and more fires than any one household has ever seen gathered in one place.

title: Murchadh Mòr brings his sons and grandsons down
summary: Murchadh Mòr comes down from the northern plain with a column of sons and grandsons that takes three days to pass any one point on the road, carrying more tent-cloth, it is said, than the valley below Dùn ìseal has ever seen brought to one place at once.

title: Eithne's knot-keeper counts every soul on the new ground
summary: Eithne comes down from the southern outpost with her own household, and her knot-keeper walks at its head with the household's cord wound about her arm, meaning to be seen keeping count of every soul who sets foot on the new ground, and does so from the first day to the last.

title: Ìomhar Dearg pitches nearest the vein
summary: Ìomhar Dearg comes down from the eastern marches nursing a hundred years' grievance over river-grazing he judges his by use if not by the king's word, and pitches his tents nearer the vein than any other line thinks wise, exactly, everyone agrees, like him.

title: Sìne nan Snaidhm keeps the cord of the whole valley
summary: Sìne nan Snaidhm, knot-keeper of the household cord at Dùn ìseal, walks the growing valley of tents checking each new fire against the cord she carries, so that within a season no soul is pitched there, of the king's blood or of any household following it down, whose count she has not kept.

title: A steward is set over every line
summary: By the second summer a steward stands over every line camped below Dùn ìseal, holding no ground and no lordship, only charged to speak for its household at the common fires and see its people fed and housed while the waiting goes on, until the valley looks less like a gathering than a town that never raised walls.

title: The host of the east begins to gather at Dùn dhearg
summary: In the spring the host of the east begins gathering at Dùn dhearg under Artair, who is said to have waited three years, since he first took up his father's holding, for the very stillness of the hill to break; word of the gathering reaches the western fires within the week.

title: Gille-Brìde and Ceallach come down to see the valley
summary: Gille-Brìde walks down out of the high valleys with Ceallach, now grown but already, though neither says it, walking more slowly than a man of his years should, and the two stand at evening looking over more fires than either has ever seen gathered at once.

title: Sìne nan Snaidhm names Gille-Brìde the one soul asking nothing
summary: Sìne nan Snaidhm tells Gille-Brìde that his name is on no cord she carries, since he has asked for no ground and no share from anyone, and that he is, that night, the only soul in the whole valley of whom that can be said.

title: The king goes down to meet the east with a handful of household
summary: Near the end of summer the king comes down from Dùn ìseal with no more than three tents' worth of his own household, going to meet the east himself, while every line camped in the valley says, each at its own fire, that it will follow him within a day or two.

title: The king sends Gille-Brìde home to the hills
summary: Gille-Brìde asks the king plainly whether he too should come down to the ford; the king tells him to go home to his own people instead, since whatever comes of it will want telling afterward by someone who was not in it, and his line has always been better at the telling than the coming.
